newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee above lows, still sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee above lows, still sharply lower.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures shaved some losses by the close on light short-covering by locals and day-traders but the market still finished weaker.
Values were dragged sharply down early in the session by origin sellers and profit takers and in response to New York's setback on Friday.
The afternoon session in London saw values stuck in a narrow range as the more-volatile New York market is closed for a national U.S. holiday.
Benchmark May dipped to below the previous $1,600 support level early in the session. But it managed to climb back to stand at $1,613 a tonne by midsession, still a $62 loss.
Front-month March took a $52 loss at $1,600. The market made its pre-opening due of $50-$70 lower.
Traders said today's retracement was seen a technical correction from an overbought condition after fresh rally late last week which took prices to a high of $1,718.
One said that further losses seemed possible with the frenzied buying which supported last week's advance was being met by increased offers.
"I still think it will come down further," said one.

The latest U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders report released on Friday for the week ended February 11 was seen as not especially notable, especially considering the time lag and price action last week, broker GNI said.
The rally in New York last week hit a peak on February 13.
All eyes were now fixed on the more relevant U.S. Green Coffee Association stock report due on Tuesday.

Barring any surprises, today's meeting among central American producer members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries to discuss export quota allocation is expected to be routine and would have little market impact.
LIFFE's certified stock data which showed a jump to 2,831 five-tonne lots in January from 1,875 in December were also largely ignored by the market. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
